### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via IApprovalService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f3e9f68e703c13e013185132f0e62ddc977f069` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a60dc15cc6ccd93955581e93d2c2ff9c1e714df0` — the merge of head `5d4cdbc23f2f43ad74b6132f90221e9e5bdd52ed` into base `1f3e9f68e703c13e013185132f0e62ddc977f069`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a60dc15cc6ccd93955581e93d2c2ff9c1e714df0 && git checkout a60dc15cc6ccd93955581e93d2c2ff9c1e714df0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1f3e9f68e703c13e013185132f0e62ddc977f069 5d4cdbc23f2f43ad74b6132f90221e9e5bdd52ed && git checkout -B drift-repro 1f3e9f68e703c13e013185132f0e62ddc977f069 && git merge --no-ff 5d4cdbc23f2f43ad74b6132f90221e9e5bdd52ed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f3e9f68e703c13e013185132f0e62ddc977f069
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1f3e9f68e703c13e013185132f0e62ddc977f069` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head 5d4cdbc2 · 2026-11-24T23:34Z

L1: ACCEPT (L1-w, zone wf-A)
Head-sha: `5d4cdbc23f2f43ad74b6132f90221e9e5bdd52ed`

No must-fix, no should-fix. **Tier H** (`docs/adr/**`, governed; the add-only arm cannot read ADR-0043, which has no Decision/Status heading), so this goes to the seat for the approver. It must not be readied, queued or armed here. It also owes an L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (non-test `packages/spec/src/**` plus a governed ADR). The claim is 7147522801, and the record follows on this head.

### Read and found right

- `l1-face.mjs --pr 37153`: 13 items clean. Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #36709` binds only this card, `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` match claim 7146025258. The changeset names `@objectstack/spec`. Floors and all checks are green: 59 success, 11 expected skips, 0 failed. `mergeable_state` clean (read through the API).
- **Scope = claim surface.** The `handleActionPage` docblock is the only hunk in `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`. ADR-0043 gets ten `+` lines and no `-` lines. The changeset was allowed by the claim, and the measured `dist/contracts/index.d.ts` shipment makes `skip-changeset` wrong. A changeset is right.
- **`Fixes` is right.** Both "done when" lines are met. The docblock names `comment` and the `400` / `reason_required` confirm-page answer, and the ADR gets an add-only note that comment capture shipped for reject in #36695 (merged, the reject-reason change).
- **Docblock, sentence by sentence, against `plugin-approvals` at this head:**
  - "a reject link's form also carries a required reason field, named `comment`": `renderConfirmPage` in `action-link-pages.ts`.
  - The POST reads `token` and `comment`, "the last of each when a field repeats". In `handleActionPage`, `form.getAll(...)` takes the last entry. The self-hosted mount uses Hono `parseBody()`, where the last value wins. Both doors agree.
  - The reject records that reason, and an approve reads no `comment` and records "Via action link": `redeemActionToken` (`comment: rejecting ? input.comment : 'Via action link'`).
  - "Missing, blank or not a string … judged by the same rule every reject door applies": `rejectReasonIssues` (`validateActionParams`, required `textarea`), shared with `decide`.
  - "Refused before the token is consumed … the same confirm page again … `400` (`reason_required`)": the check sits before the `consumed_at` update, and `actionRedemptionPage` returns `{ status: 400, renderConfirmPage(refusal) }`.
  - "A dead link is judged first and still told on its result page": `resolveActionToken` runs first, and dead outcomes get a `200` result page.
  - `@param` / `@returns`: match.
- **ADR note.** It sits after Non-goals and states the same facts. "The first Non-goals bullet above stands as written for v1" keeps the v1 record unedited, which is the add-only intent.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.** "Documentation only; no type, schema or export changes": true, the hunk is comment text only. The three bullets (reason field with last-of-each parsing; missing, blank or non-string answered with the confirm page, `400`, `reason_required`, token not consumed, a dead link still `200`; approve records "Via action link"): each matches the code read above.
- **Tests.** The spec build, typecheck and test suite ran with real output. There is a positive control for the `.d.ts` shipment ("The token is the only credential" is found beside the new sentence). No ablation applies (text only).

### Notes (not findings)

- **Same file as #37145.** The rework round on PR #37145 (#37041) now edits the `getRecordLock` / `getRecordLocks` docblocks in this same `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`. That is a different region (around line 1100, against this PR's around line 1391), so git merges them cleanly. Whichever lands second should re-read its own docblock after rebasing. `overlap-check` may report a file-level hit.
- The PR body has no opening `repo:objectstack#3 · …` signature line. The dev records this as a deviation, because the order puts the two attribution lines first. The closing `signed:` trailer carries it. PR #37145 puts the signature as line 3. That is a placement choice for the seat, not a defect.
- The open question (split vs one Tier H PR) is the seat's call. Either way the spec half carries the same L2 record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5d4cdbc23f2f43ad74b6132f90221e9e5bdd52ed`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts, docs/adr/0043-actionable-approval-links.md + none
Security-touching: yes

Security-touching is `yes` because the changed hunks teach credential behaviour: when the action-link token is and is not consumed, that a refused reject leaves the link live and reusable, and what the token-authenticated POST reads. The path names do not show this; the adopting seat adds the `security` label.

The code these texts describe is outside the diff (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`, `approvals-plugin.ts`, `action-link-pages.ts`). It was read at this head to judge them and is not reviewed. The diff holds no implementing file, hence `+ none`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. The diff to `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` is confined to the docblock of `IApprovalService.handleActionPage`; the member signature (a `Request` in, a promise of a `Response` out) is untouched, and no type, schema, export or zod shape moves. Right.
- Public surface: the docblock text ships in the `@objectstack/spec` declaration output, so the published text changes while the published types do not. Right, and it is what the changeset declares.
- Metadata protocol: nothing a metadata author can write changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- ADR-0043: ten added lines, no removed or edited line, placed after the Non-goals list. Add-only, right. The Status line and every decision row are untouched.
- Behaviour: none moves. No test is added and none is owed for a text-only change; the behaviour the text describes is already pinned on `main` by `action-page-member.integration.test.ts` (blank reason answers 400 on both doors, the token survives, the last repeated field wins).
- Gate verdicts on this head, read from the 70 check-runs: 59 success, 11 skipped, no failure. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Spec property liveness` and `Check Documentation Links` are all success. The skipped runs are opt-in or path-filtered jobs (`Lint UI`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the queue verdicts, the temporal and upgrade harnesses), none of them a gate this diff owes.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36709-action-page-contract-reject-reason.md` releases `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. That matches what the diff publishes: documentation text inside a released package's declaration output, with no type change. `skip-changeset` would be wrong, because the label is for a diff that publishes nothing, and this one publishes changed docblock text. `patch` is the level AGENTS.md assigns to `Metadata-protocol: none`.

Clause-②: no — stated in both the PR body and the changeset body, line-initial, with no arm. Right: no accept-set is widened or narrowed. The reject-reason narrowing itself landed with PR #36695 and is not re-published here.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, changeset added although the order said "only if a gate asks": answered, correct. `Check Changeset` needs a changeset or the skip label, and the skip label does not fit a diff that publishes.
- Deviations on the PR body footer and signature placement: PR-body prose, outside this record's scope; no contract effect.
- `open_questions`, landing route A (one Tier H PR) or B (split spec half from ADR half): answered from the contract side, escalated for the route. The two texts describe one behaviour and agree with each other and with the code, so nothing in the contract asks for a split, and a split changes no text. The dev's reading of the tier is consistent with the diff: the spec path and the `@objectstack/spec` changeset are outside the low-risk arm, and ADR-0043 has no Decision or Status heading. Whether to hand one PR to the approver or split it is a landing decision for the owning seat and the approver; this record covers the head as it stands and would not cover a split head.
- Out-of-scope note, ADR-0043 has no Decision or Status heading so the add-only arm can never accept a note to it: a property of the record and the arm, correctly not fixed here. It is a candidate follow-up card for the seat, not a finding on this PR.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`, judged sentence by sentence against the code at this head:

- "a reject link's form also carries a required reason field, named `comment`": holds. `renderConfirmPage` renders a `textarea` with `name="comment"` and `required` for a reject, and no such field for an approve.
- "`POST` ... reads the token from the `token` field ... and, for a reject link, the reason from its `comment` field (the last of each when a field repeats)": holds on both doors. `handleActionPage` takes the last entry of `form.getAll('token')` and of `form.getAll('comment')`; the self-hosted mount uses Hono's `parseBody` without `all`, which keeps the last value of a repeated key. The parity test pins this.
- The redemption chain order, with "a reject recording that reason as its comment": holds. `redeemActionToken` resolves the token, consumes it, then calls `decide` with `comment` set to the posted text for a reject.
- "An approve link reads no `comment` and records the fixed comment "Via action link"": holds as observable behaviour. The door parses the field on every POST, but `redeemActionToken` ignores it unless the token's action is `reject`, and an approve records the fixed text.
- "missing, blank or not a string — judged by the same rule every reject door applies": holds. `rejectReasonIssues` is the one judge, called by both `decide` and `redeemActionToken`; it runs `validateActionParams` against a required `textarea` param, which refuses an absent value, a blank one and a non-string one (a file part, for example).
- "refused before the token is consumed ... status `400` (the redemption outcome `reason_required`) ... the link stays live": holds. The `reason_required` return precedes the `sys_approval_token` update, and `actionRedemptionPage` maps it to the confirm page with `refusal: 'reason_required'` and status 400 for both doors.
- "A dead link is judged first and is still told on its result page": holds. `resolveActionToken` runs before the reason check, so an invalid, consumed, expired, decided or reassigned link answers its 200 result page whether or not a reason came with it.
- "The `400` above refuses the input, not the link", and the `@param` / `@returns` lines: consistent with the above and with the unchanged "never as an error status" sentence.

Attempts to break it: a reject link that is dead and also has no reason (200 result page, as the text says); a repeated `comment` whose last value is blank (400, as the text says); a whitespace-only reason (400, pinned by the test); a non-form body (no token, told invalid, 200, already described on the plugin side and not contradicted here); an approve link posted with a `comment` (ignored, fixed comment recorded). None contradicts a sentence. Leaving the token unconsumed after a refused reject does not weaken ADR-0043's axes: nothing is decided, the token stays bound to one request, one action and one approver, and the TTL, the single use on a real decision and the slot re-check all still apply.

`docs/adr/0043-actionable-approval-links.md`, against its first consumer (`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`) and the card: the note states what the plugin does, names PR #36695 as the card asks, leaves the first Non-goals bullet standing as the v1 record, and says approve is unchanged. It agrees with the docblock on every shared point (field name, the three refusal cases, status 400, token not consumed, fixed approve comment). Both "Done when" lines of the card are met.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — the ADR note says a POST whose `comment` is missing, blank or not a string is answered the confirm page with `400`, without the docblock's qualifier that a dead link is judged first and still gets its result page. The surrounding sentences scope it to a live reject link, and the Redeem bullet above already orders the checks, so no reader is misled. Left as an accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — one reflowed docblock line ("expired, consumed or no longer live, the explanatory result page. ⛔ A `GET`") now runs past the wrap width of its neighbours. Cosmetic; left as an accepted deviation.
